title: Kid Rena, Joe Rena and playing blues at fourteen
summary: Punch wanted to stay in the home to learn music but was refused; at fourteen he played only blues for dances.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Kid Rene. Kid Rene was there then? Sure. Kid Rene. Was that before? I left him. I didn't stay there. But I wanted to stay because they would learn music, see. And I wanted to stay, but they wouldn't let me stay because I come to the country, see.
What about Joe Rene? Was he in the home or out?
Well, yeah, he was in that world, too.
Yeah, but not with you, huh? No, no. And he was in the brass band, too, though, wasn't he? Yeah, that's right, the Zulus. We got an interview with him, too. Excuse me.
Could you play... You were supposed to have taken a... What? Music at 14. So you... When you were in the home, did you play...
Well, yeah, well, I played the blues and things. Nothing but the blues at 14. I know nothing but blues. But the people like it. They play dances. Play different kind of blues. They like it.
